schema_diagram.description: Entity-Relationship diagram showing database schema and relationships
schema_diagram.content:
erDiagram
    DISTRICT ||--o{ ACCOUNT : "has"
    DISP ||--o{ CARD : "has"
    DISTRICT ||--o{ CLIENT : "has"
    CLIENT ||--o{ DISP : "has"
    ACCOUNT ||--o{ DISP : "has"
    ACCOUNT ||--o{ TRANS : "has"

    DISP {
        int disp_id PK
        int client_id FK
        int account_id FK
        text type
    }
    DISTRICT {
        int district_id PK
        text A2
        text A3
        text A4
        text A5
        text A6
        text A7
        int A8
        int A9
        float A10
        int A11
        float A12
        float A13
        int A14
        int A15
        int A16
    }
    LOAN {
        int loan_id PK
        int account_id
        datetime date
        int amount
        int duration
        float payments
        text status
    }
    ORDER {
        int order_id PK
        int account_id
        text bank_to
        int account_to
        float amount
        text k_symbol
    }
    TRANS {
        int trans_id PK
        int account_id FK
        datetime date
        text type
        text operation
        int amount
        int balance
        text k_symbol
        text bank
        int account
    }
    ACCOUNT {
        int account_id PK
        int district_id FK
        text frequency
        datetime date
    }
    CARD {
        int card_id PK
        int disp_id FK
        text type
        datetime issued
    }
    CLIENT {
        int client_id PK
        text gender
        datetime birth_date
        int district_id FK
    }

columns.name: date
columns.official_meaning: the creation date of the account

account_id_meaning.content: Primary key, unique identifier for each account. Values range from 1 to 11382 with gaps; 4500 total accounts.

date_meaning.content: Account creation date. Stored as ISO date text 'YYYY-MM-DD' (with optional timestamp); NOT the YYMMDD format described in the official reference. Range: 1993-01-01 to 1997-12-29.

district_id_meaning.content: Location (branch district) where the account was opened. Foreign key to district.district_id. No orphan records; values range 1-77.

frequency_meaning.content: Account statement frequency. POPLATEK MESICNE = monthly, POPLATEK TYDNE = weekly, POPLATEK PO OBRATU = per transaction.

frequency_values.content: POPLATEK MESICNE=monthly(4167, 92.6%), POPLATEK TYDNE=weekly(240, 5.3%), POPLATEK PO OBRATU=per transaction(93, 2.1%)

columns.name: issued
columns.official_meaning: the date when the credit card issued

disp.name: disp
disp.description: This table links each client to an account and defines their disposition type (owner or disponent) for that account.

columns.name: disp_id
columns.official_meaning: unique number of identifying this row of record

business_rules.content: type: "OWNER" : "USER" : "DISPONENT" commonsense evidence: the account can only have the right to issue permanent orders or apply for loans

client_id_meaning.content: Client identifier; each row links one client to one account. Here 5369 unique clients = 5369 total rows, so each client occurs only once in this table.

disp_id_meaning.content: Primary key; unique row identifier for each client-account disposition record.

type_values.content: OWNER=4500(83.8%), DISPONENT=869(16.2%); no USER values present

A3_meaning.content: Czech regional grouping (NUTS-like) of districts: Prague, central Bohemia, south Bohemia, west Bohemia, north Bohemia, east Bohemia, south Moravia, north Moravia.

A3_values.content: Prague=1(1%), central Bohemia=12(16%), south Moravia=14(18%), north Moravia=11(14%), east Bohemia=11(14%), west Bohemia=10(13%), north Bohemia=10(13%), south Bohemia=8(10%)

loan.name: loan
loan.description: This table tracks loan contracts and their current status, including whether they are finished, running, or in debt.

columns.name: loan_id
columns.official_meaning: the id number identifying the loan data

columns.name: account_id
columns.official_meaning: the id number identifying the account

columns.name: date
columns.official_meaning: the date when the loan is approved

business_rules.content: amount: unit：US dollar | duration: unit：month | payments: unit：month | status: 'A' stands for contract finished, no problems; 'B' stands for contract finished, loan not paid; 'C' stands for running contract, OK so far; 'D' stands for running contract, client in debt

status_values.content: A=contract finished, no problems(203, 29.8%), B=contract finished, loan not paid(31, 4.5%), C=running contract, OK so far(403, 59.1%), D=running contract, client in debt(45, 6.6%)

business_rules.content: account_to: each bank has unique two-letter code

quality_issues.description: Contains 1379 empty string values in addition to NULLs

business_rules.content: amount: Unit：USD | balance: Unit：USD | bank: each bank has unique two-letter code

account.account_id→disp.account_id.description: account → disp via disp.account_id [1:N]; selecting child after JOIN can duplicate parent rows

account.district_id→district.district_id.description: account.district_id → district.district_id [N:1]; avg 58.4 child rows/parent — JOIN may multiply rows; use DISTINCT when listing unique parents

disp.account_id→account.account_id.description: disp.account_id → account.account_id [N:1]; avg 1.2 child rows/parent — JOIN may multiply rows; use DISTINCT when listing unique parents

district.district_id→account.district_id.description: district → account via account.district_id [1:N]; selecting child after JOIN can duplicate parent rows

account.district_id.note: FK → district.district_id [N:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names. Parent→child is 1:N: JOIN from parent multiplies rows; DISTINCT if listing unique parents.

card.disp_id.note: FK → disp.disp_id [1:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names.

client.district_id.note: FK → district.district_id [N:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names.

disp.account_id.note: FK → account.account_id [N:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names. Parent→child is 1:N: JOIN from parent multiplies rows; DISTINCT if listing unique parents.

disp.client_id.note: FK → client.client_id [1:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names.

trans.account_id.note: FK → account.account_id [N:1]. Stores ID, not display name — JOIN parent to get names.
